flashcard_questions.q: How many ships did Spain send in the Armada?
How many men sailed aboard the Armada?
How many soldiers waited in the Netherlands under the Duke of Parma?
Which treaty of 1585 made Elizabeth openly back the Dutch rebels?
What nickname was given to Drake’s 1587 raid on Cadiz?
flashcard_questions.a: Singeing the King of Spain’s beard.

flashcard_questions.q: Whose execution in February 1587 ended Philip’s diplomatic hopes?
Who commanded the English fleet against the Armada?
Why was Medina Sidonia a poor choice of commander?
flashcard_questions.a: He had no naval experience, having been chosen for his high rank.

flashcard_questions.q: What did the English send into the Spanish fleet at Calais at midnight?
Why did the fireships break the Spanish crescent formation?
flashcard_questions.a: Panicking captains cut their anchor ropes and scattered.

flashcard_questions.q: In which battle did the English attack the scattered Armada at close range?
How many Armada ships made it back to Spain?
What was written on the medal Elizabeth had struck after the victory?
What did Elizabeth say at Tilbury about her body and her heart?
flashcard_questions.a: “I know I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a king.”

notes: 15 cards: 6 figure (ships, men, soldiers, fireships, survivors), 4 person-to-significance, 3 cause-effect, 2 source/quotation. Lesson supplies no glossary, so all cards come from the body text.
